No previous report is rewritten or rescored. The original law, cutoffs, fixed exterior, determining set, C1 and mean are kept.

DISTINGUISH THE TWO QUANTITIES. Write e(g) for the ACTUAL already fixed CMP119 small-background indicator amplitude called epsilon1 there, with e(g)=A0 g1(log g1^-2)^p0. Write e_var for the positive regularity/enlargement parameter in CMP102 condition7 and172. The latter theorem is quantified for any sufficiently small positive parameter; using its bounds with e_var=K e does not change the physical chi1 indicator, beta/coupling law, integration domain, gauge or coarse constraint. It only bounds the same configurations by a possibly larger auxiliary regularity class. This use is legal only after their ACTUAL data satisfy the class with a uniform fixed K. It cannot manufacture regularity of an arbitrary fixed exterior as e tends to zero.

EXACT REFINEMENT CHECK. On compatible unit blocks of side L, define R(V)=Q1^*V exactly as source1191.3: fine links inside a block are identity, links crossing a mu-face carry the corresponding V_mu(y), with inverse values on reverse orientations. Consider an elementary fine mu-nu plaquette. If it crosses neither block face its holonomy is I. If it crosses just one directional face the two equal V factors cancel exactly. If it crosses both, its ordered holonomy is the coarse plaquette V_mu(y)V_nu(y+mu)V_mu(y+nu)^-1 V_nu(y)^-1. This uses no commuting of group elements, no flat coarse data or global near-identity gauge. An entire coarse corridor through R(V) has transport V(c), so the original consistent covariant group average returns exactly V(c).

Consequently in a mixed determining set whose new fine stratum is a union of the original full blocks, new fine data R(V) and retained coarse data V satisfy the original mixed substitution in CMP1027 with the SAME coarse plaquette bound: when a missing coarse bond is replaced by its average of lower-stratum fields, that average is exactly V(c). This is a category-by-category equality of data, not a continuous-complement convention. Old fine exterior data are unchanged. To use the equality for the ACTUAL patched determining set of1191.21, retain the original maximal-domain construction, block compatibility and the actual clearance of Gamma from old fine exterior strata. The1739 geometric coverage is a conditional sufficient witness, not a newly changed domain. No plaquette meeting an unchanged old fine stratum may be silently replaced by this refinement argument; those plaquettes retain the old source condition7 obligation.

LOCAL COARSE REGULARITY CONSUMER. On each actual required good two-block patch with local minimum U1,D and original mean M^1(U1,D)=V, choose actual reference corridor paths for the four coarse edges. Their coarse square loop and alternative corridor comparison surfaces lie in the same fixed two-block box. Retain A_box=16d^2 L^2 from1737 for these coordinate-strip surfaces and all actual fixed path transports. If local fine plaquettes satisfy |U1,D(dp)-I|<=e L^-2, real-unitary product telescoping bounds the reference loop by A_box e L^-2. Each of the four actual averaged coarse transports differs from its reference by at most C_A A_box e L^-2, using the SAME covariant relative mean, consistency and its admitted Lipschitz chart. Four-factor telescoping gives

 |V(dp_coarse)-I| <= K_coarse e,
 K_coarse=(1+4C_A) A_box L^-2.                         (1)

This is a local finite-carrier comparison of the actual mean. It retains the mean chart and source indicator membership; it is not an assumption that fine curvature bounds absolute links. A pure-gauge phase cancels through covariance. It needs the entire comparison surfaces inside the original good patch, not just its central plaquette. No claim is made that every original coarse plaquette globally is good; only actual patches on which the source small-background indicator holds are covered.

Combine this with the1737/1739 actual relative fine-data bound, on their same admitted patches,

 ||B0|| <= K_rel e,
 K_rel=2 C_log(1+2C_M)(1+C_A) A_box L^-2.               (2)

The norm and log/mean chart margins are retained. Equation(2) uses the original global-vs-local curvature comparison, not a new proof of that locality statement. If all new mixed base plaquettes are of the refinement type just checked, (1) pays their condition7 with e_var>K_coarse e. Unchanged old plaquettes retain their actual prior bound K_old e if one is already certified. K_old is NOT defined by a supremum which could diverge with volume/coupling, and is not invented to include arbitrary large-field fixed data.

Choose ONCE, before varying coupling, a fixed finite

 K > max(1,K_coarse,K_rel/C1,K_old), e_var(g)=K e(g).    (3)

The K_old entry is used only for actual unchanged condition7 plaquettes with such a uniform witness. If there is no witness, the corresponding admission stays open and (3) supplies none. On covered data, (3) yields strict base regularity <e_var and ||B0||<C1 e_var. Thus the latter fixed-ratio test need not demand K_rel<C1 when e_var and physical e are not required to be equal. This does not improve that ratio by taking g smaller or increasing C1; it uses the theorem's own quantified regularity parameter to dominate the actual data. It is an auxiliary majorant choice with all costs retained, not a change to the physical law.

For 0<=t<=1, let V_t=exp(itB0)V_base on the changed fine data, with coarse/fixed exterior entries unchanged. It is unnecessary to demand that EVERY V_t satisfies condition7 with the original e_var: SectionG takes a base V_base satisfying7 and a near-identity relative factor in172.
